title: UFO Disclosure 2026: Department Of War Releases 8th Batch Of Files; Here's How To Access
excerpt: The latest tranche of documents disclosing UAP activities around the world is here, but we haven't seen concrete proof of ETs or alien phenomena that UFOlogists claim to have evidence of, but . . .the UFO fatigue is real
content:
The Department of War released the eighth tranche of declassified UFO files on Friday, adding 40 documents and three videos to the treasure trove. The batch was unsealed under the Presidential Unsealing and Reporting System for UAP Encounters, or PURSUE, which was set up after an executive order from President Donald Trump. Most of the papers dropped in the latest disclosure dates to the 1950s. All three videos in the 8th batch were submitted by US Central Command to the All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office, aka AARO.

The @DeptofWar has released the eighth tranche of records, reinforcing our commitment under PURSUE to increase transparency by responsibly releasing information. To view Release 8: https://t.co/OqkuFL2iFN

— All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office (@DoW_AARO) November 20, 2026

UFOs & Psych Warfare

The three videos (now viral on socials) date from 2020, 2023, and 2026. They were shot by sensors on US military platforms in the Middle East. They show white dots crossing the frame. In the 2026 clip, which runs 54 seconds, the sensor tracks several of them.

The oldest item in the drop is a 16-page CIA file from fall 1952. Director Walter Bedell Smith told the Psychological Strategy Board that UFO issues had implications for psychological warfare. The attached study counted about 1,500 official sightings since 1947, 250 of them in July 1952, of which the Air Force left 20 percent unexplained. Wonder why!

What’s The Deal With The Las Vegas Paper?

Then there is the Las Vegas paper. A 538-page report (available here) by Bigelow Aerospace Advanced Space Studies, written in July 2009 for the Defense Intelligence Agency, proposed an underground vault at the company's North Las Vegas site. It was meant to hold recovered hardware and biological samples. Whether it was ever built is unclear, since later reports never mention it. A copy leaked online last year; however, this is the first time the Pentagon has published the same.

Avi Loeb Reacts To 8th Batch Of UFO Files

Harvard astrophysicist and chairman of the White House UAP Science Advisory Council, Avi Loeb, in his last interview with Fox News, remarked that the batch has no clear evidence of non-human technology. He said there is no digital data to rule out that the 1953 object reported by Lockheed chief engineer Kelly Johnson was a black project.

On the three videos, Loeb said his council found most objects flicker eight times per second, which is what flapping wings produce.

You will see all the current 8 tranche in a row. Click on the batch you wanna dig and viola! Happy tumbling down the rabbit hole.
